source: Irisin, a skeletal-muscle secreted myokine, facilitates muscle-bone crosstalk and skeletal remodeling in part by its action on osteoblasts and osteocytes.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro osteoclast differentiation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Forced expression of the irisin precursor Fndc5 in transgenic C57BL/6J mice resulted in lower bone mass at three ages.

claim: Forced expression of the irisin precursor Fndc5 in transgenic C57BL/6J mice resulted in greater in vitro osteoclastogenesis from Fndc5-transgenic bone marrow progenitors.

claim: Irisin acts directly on osteoclast progenitors to increase differentiation and promote bone resorption.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings regarding irisin's physiological role.

source: Markedly lower cortical bone area was observed by µCT at younger ages in Fndc5-transgenic (TG) mice compared to wild type (WT) (2 and 4.5 months), with significant decreases in trabecular bone volume fraction at 2 (p<0.0001) and 4.5 months (p=0.0003) and in cortical thickness at 2 months (p<0.0001; Figure 4b, Source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Fndc5-transgenic mice showed significant decreases in trabecular bone volume fraction at 4.5 months (p=0.0003).
source: Markedly lower cortical bone area was observed by µCT at younger ages in Fndc5-transgenic (TG) mice compared to wild type (WT) (2 and 4.5 months), with significant decreases in trabecular bone volume fraction at 2 (p<0.0001) and 4.5 months (p=0.0003) and in cortical thickness at 2 months (p<0.0001; Figure 4b, Source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Fndc5-transgenic mice showed significant decreases in cortical thickness at 2 months (p<0.0001).
source: Markedly lower cortical bone area was observed by µCT at younger ages in Fndc5-transgenic (TG) mice compared to wild type (WT) (2 and 4.5 months), with significant decreases in trabecular bone volume fraction at 2 (p<0.0001) and 4.5 months (p=0.0003) and in cortical thickness at 2 months (p<0.0001; Figure 4b, Source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by µCT data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Significant decreases in the number of osteoblasts per bone perimeter were observed in Fndc5-transgenic mice at 2 months (p=0.05).
source: Significant decreases in both the number of osteoblasts per bone perimeter (p=0.05) and bone formation rate (p=0.0046) were observed only at 2 months, and not at 13 months.
evidence: This is supported by histomorphometry data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Significant decreases in bone formation rate were observed in Fndc5-transgenic mice at 2 months (p=0.0046).
source: Significant decreases in both the number of osteoblasts per bone perimeter (p=0.05) and bone formation rate (p=0.0046) were observed only at 2 months, and not at 13 months.
evidence: This is supported by histomorphometry data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: In vitro osteoblast differentiation from bone marrow mesenchymal cells harvested at 2–3 months did not differ by genotype in Fndc5-transgenic mice.
source: However, in vitro osteoblast differentiation from bone marrow mesenchymal cells harvested at 2–3 months did not differ by genotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro osteoblast differentiation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Primary bone marrow progenitors isolated from Fndc5-transgenic mice at 2–3 months demonstrated markedly greater osteoclastogenic potential compared to the wild type (p<0.0001).
source: However, primary bone marrow progenitors isolated from Fndc5-transgenic mice at 2–3 months demonstrated markedly greater osteoclastogenic potential compared to the wild type, yielding significantly higher numbers of osteoclasts that were qualitatively larger than controls during in vitro differentiation (p<0.0001; Figure 4d, Source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro osteoclast differentiation data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Irisin plays an important role in regulating bone remodeling by directly acting on osteoclasts to promote differentiation and resorption.
source: This study demonstrates that irisin plays an important role in regulating bone remodeling not only by stimulating osteoblasts and osteocytes as previously described, but by also directly acting on osteoclasts to promote differentiation and resorption.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The stimulatory effect of irisin on osteoclasts occurred with either intermittent or continuous irisin exposure across a range of physiologic concentrations previously reported in humans.
source: This stimulatory effect was observed across multiple experiments with primary murine progenitors and the RAW 264.7 macrophage cell line and occurred with either intermittent or continuous irisin exposure across a range of physiologic concentrations previously reported in humans (Jedrychowski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and a citation to prior research on irisin concentrations.

claim: Both recruitment and differentiation of more osteoclast progenitors with irisin treatment appeared to be driving factors of enhanced bone resorption.
source: Furthermore, we found that both recruitment and differentiation of more osteoclast progenitors with irisin treatment appeared to be driving factors of enhanced bone resorption, based on in situ studies on native dentin as well as synthetic calcium phosphate and collagen substrates (Figure 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the resorption assay data.

claim: Several osteoclast-secretory factors known to stimulate osteoblasts were significantly upregulated by irisin treatment.
source: In addition, several osteoclast-secretory factors known to stimulate osteoblasts were significantly upregulated, suggesting that the direct actions of irisin on this cell type may have further impact on cell signaling to enhance coupled remodeling (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The direct actions of irisin on osteoclasts may have further impact on cell signaling to enhance coupled remodeling.
source: In addition, several osteoclast-secretory factors known to stimulate osteoblasts were significantly upregulated, suggesting that the direct actions of irisin on this cell type may have further impact on cell signaling to enhance coupled remodeling (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the gene expression findings.

claim: The relative contribution of osteoclastogenesis to the skeletal phenotype cannot be resolved in the Fndc5-transgenic genetic model.
source: The relative contribution of osteoclastogenesis to the skeletal phenotype cannot be resolved in our genetic model.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the genetic model.

claim: Early decreases in osteoblast numbers and bone formation rate were observed by histomorphometry at 2 months of age in the Fndc5-transgenic mouse.
source: While early decreases in osteoblast numbers and bone formation rate were observed by histomorphometry at 2 months of age in the transgenic mouse, these metrics became equivalent to controls at 13 months, whereas a trend for increased osteoclast numbers was noted at 13 months.
evidence: This is supported by histomorphometry data.

claim: Osteoblast numbers and bone formation rate became equivalent to controls at 13 months in Fndc5-transgenic mice.
source: While early decreases in osteoblast numbers and bone formation rate were observed by histomorphometry at 2 months of age in the transgenic mouse, these metrics became equivalent to controls at 13 months, whereas a trend for increased osteoclast numbers was noted at 13 months.
evidence: This is supported by histomorphometry data.

claim: A trend for increased osteoclast numbers was noted at 13 months in Fndc5-transgenic mice.
source: While early decreases in osteoblast numbers and bone formation rate were observed by histomorphometry at 2 months of age in the transgenic mouse, these metrics became equivalent to controls at 13 months, whereas a trend for increased osteoclast numbers was noted at 13 months.
evidence: This is supported by histomorphometry data.

claim: Continuous exogenous treatment with 10 ng/mL irisin had no observable effect on osteoblast differentiation or mineralization.
source: Additionally, we have found that continuous exogenous treatment with 10 ng/mL irisin used to stimulate in vitro osteoclast differentiation from wild type progenitors had no observable effect on osteoblast differentiation or mineralization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro osteoblast differentiation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the forced expression model, irisin may act at early stages to reduce bone mass by suppressing osteoblast-mediated bone formation.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate a clear action of irisin on the osteoclast, but further suggest that in this forced expression model, irisin may act at early stages to reduce bone mass by suppressing osteoblast-mediated bone formation, while the later and persistent effects on bone turnover may be more focused on the osteoclast.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings from the transgenic mouse model.

claim: In the forced expression model, the later and persistent effects of irisin on bone turnover may be more focused on the osteoclast.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate a clear action of irisin on the osteoclast, but further suggest that in this forced expression model, irisin may act at early stages to reduce bone mass by suppressing osteoblast-mediated bone formation, while the later and persistent effects on bone turnover may be more focused on the osteoclast.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings from the transgenic mouse model.

claim: Both dose and duration of irisin exposure may be critical determinants of the skeletal response.
source: it is important to note that both dose and duration of irisin exposure may be critical determinants of the skeletal response and hence be responsible for phenotypic differences.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed differences in experimental outcomes.

claim: The activity of the Mck promoter for Fndc5 is very high at 2 months but waned with age.
source: For example, from our gene expression studies, it is clear that the activity of the Mck promoter for Fndc5 is very high at 2 months but waned with age, albeit still maintaining relatively increased levels (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Supraphysiologic levels of irisin suppressed osteoclastogenesis in vitro.
source: This exposure difference may impact skeletal cell responsiveness as noted by an earlier study demonstrating suppressed osteoclastogenesis in vitro with supraphysiologic levels of irisin (Marino et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: 20 ng/mL irisin had little effect on osteoclast number in vitro.
source: Similarly, we found that 20 ng/mL irisin had little effect on osteoclast number in vitro (Figure 1b)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Doses of irisin equal or exceeding 100 ng/mL showed reduced osteoclast numbers.
source: and initial experiments with doses of irisin equal or exceeding 100 ng/mL actually showed reduced osteoclast numbers (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations mentioned but not shown in detail.

claim: Irisin concentrations in humans are approximately 2–4 ng/mL as measured by mass spectrometry.
source: Our previous work employed mass spectrometry to demonstrate that irisin concentrations in humans are approximately 2–4 ng/mL (Jedrychowski et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research using mass spectrometry.

claim: Even low concentrations of irisin down to 2 ng/mL significantly increase osteoclast number.
source: While we primarily employed a concentration of 10 ng/mL to represent a robust but physiologically relevant in vitro stimulus, we also demonstrated that even low concentrations down to 2 ng/mL significantly increase osteoclast number.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Both dosing and timing relative to developmental age may be determinants of irisin's function as a dynamic signaling molecule in the skeleton.
source: Thus, both dosing and timing relative to developmental age may be determinants of irisin's function as a dynamic signaling molecule in the skeleton, and its actions on specific bone cell types.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The relatively narrow dose range for stimulating osteoclastogenesis could have physiologic implications since exercise induces rapid changes in serum calcium.
source: It should be noted that the relatively narrow dose range for stimulating osteoclastogenesis could have physiologic implications since exercise induces rapid changes in serum calcium (Ng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation to prior research on exercise and serum calcium.

claim: If irisin targets both osteoclasts and osteocytes, it may serve as another counter-regulatory hormone to maintain serum calcium during the early phases of exercise much like parathyroid hormone.
source: If irisin targets both osteoclasts and osteocytes, it may serve as another counter-regulatory hormone to maintain serum calcium during the early phases of exercise much like parathyroid hormone (Ng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of irisin's potential physiological role, supported by a citation.

claim: Irisin mediates muscle-bone crosstalk by regulating bone remodeling.
source: Taken together, our studies provide more evidence that irisin mediates muscle-bone crosstalk by regulating bone remodeling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Irisin is able to act directly on all key cell types of the bone remodeling unit.
source: While further studies are necessary to fully elucidate irisin's mechanism of action on the osteoclast and to resolve contrasting cellular effects observed between cell types and experimental models, it remains clear that this myokine is a potent regulator of bone remodeling that is able to both act directly on all key cell types of the bone remodeling unit, and potentially modulate signaling between them.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and prior research.

claim: Irisin can potentially modulate signaling between key cell types of the bone remodeling unit.
source: While further studies are necessary to fully elucidate irisin's mechanism of action on the osteoclast and to resolve contrasting cellular effects observed between cell types and experimental models, it remains clear that this myokine is a potent regulator of bone remodeling that is able to both act directly on all key cell types of the bone remodeling unit, and potentially modulate signaling between them.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of irisin's potential role in bone remodeling.
